solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ship is steadied by this thing which is round a stone

parts.note: a ball is the archetypal round thing
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A sailor's riddle about some round object steadying a ship with a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first half is a descriptive definition; 'thing which is round' is a roundabout way of naming a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy material carried low in a hull to give a vessel stability.

clue.text: Eliot's opening on sitting under brown shrub seen in poetry

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece sitting under another follows it

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brown

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of the poet's name is used

parts.note: the first letter of the poet's name
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: How T S Eliot's verse begins, beneath a brown bush in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Brere is an old poetic spelling of briar, a prickly shrub.

clue.text: Polynesian superman's indefinable quality set in gold

indicators.note: something set in metal is mounted inside it, like a stone in a ring

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
it is that indefinable appeal, as in she has got it

explanation.surface: A South Seas hero's mysterious charisma, rendered in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In Polynesia an aitu is a demigod or spirit, a being more than human.

clue.text: Lodge in luxury college, cohab should ring

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the partner goes around the college letter

parts.note: a cohab is a cohabitant, a partner one lives with
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: Students sharing digs at a posh college should get engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests an engagement ring, but it means surround: the live-in lover wraps around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To live in clover is to enjoy great comfort and luxury, so to dwell or lodge in luxury.

clue.text: Colouring anecdotal collection with extreme spinning

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person

indicators.note: spinning round turns a piece about, so it is read backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extreme

explanation.surface: A dye made from a gathering of tales, given a wild twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatto (annatto) is an orange-red dye from a tropical tree, used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: The Tube left to go by cerebration?

parts.note: the tube is slang for television, the telly or tele
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A London Underground train leaving, apparently powered by thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: To teleport is to travel instantly, as if by mental power alone, rather than by any vehicle.

clue.text: Lit up and ready to burst

indicators.note: something that bursts flies apart, so the word before it is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something illuminated and on the point of exploding, like a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayed means sending out rays, that is, shining or lit up with beams.

clue.text: Hinder nurse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the adjective, further back
second meaning: to bring up or raise a child

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hinder' looks like the verb to obstruct; it is the adjective meaning further behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear is both the adjective for the back part and the verb meaning to bring up or tend young.

clue.text: Concert is into morphing zydeco comp, perhaps

parts.note: concert in the sense of agreement, as in acting in concert

indicators.note: morphing is changing shape, so those letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gig turning into a zydeco composition.
explanation.walkthrough: Zydeco is a Louisiana Creole music led by the accordion; comp is short for accompanist.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordionist is the typical accompanist in a zydeco band, so the example fits with 'perhaps'.

clue.text: A set of overseas selectors heading west of Wishaw

indicators.note: a set of letters drawn out of the words that follow, rather than the whole words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Foreign team selectors travelling west from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Wishaw is a town in Lanarkshire, signalling a Scots word; something easterly comes from the east and so heads west.
explanation.definitionFit: Eassel is Scots for easterly, describing what moves from the east towards the west.

clue.text: Harry insulting commie makes steady progress

parts.note: to dog or harry is to pursue persistently
Trot is a dismissive word for a Trotskyist

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry abuses a communist and gets on steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name; it is the verb to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is a gentle easy trot, so a steady unhurried pace.

clue.text: Racket in fake tax-man's district

indicators.note: one word sits inside another, so the noise goes within the fake

parts.note: to rig is to fake or fix, as in a rigged result
a din is a loud noise, a racket

explanation.surface: A noisy scam in the area covered by a corrupt tax collector.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives riding as a district visited by an excise officer, besides its familiar sense of a division of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records riding as the district patrolled by an excise officer, a tax collector's beat.

clue.text: Unconventional unit led agent to weaken?

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An irregular unit guided a spy, perhaps to undermine something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' suggests a spy but means a substance doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A diluent is a substance used to thin or dilute something, reducing its strength.

clue.text: Italian company on greeting

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
I is the international abbreviation for Italy
Chambers gives a as an old preposition meaning on, as in abed or afoot

explanation.surface: An Italian firm says hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The I and the A, read together, sit within the company abbreviation; the Italian flavour of the surface fits the answer, which is the Italian hello or goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an informal salutation borrowed from Italian, used both on meeting and on parting.

clue.text: Adult clumsily cleans daggers

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: doing something clumsily makes a mess of it, so the following letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up making a poor job of wiping knives.
explanation.definitionFit: An anlace is a medieval short two-edged dagger or knife worn at the belt.

clue.text: In error lead oblivion and endless opportunity in decay

indicators.note: the combined pieces are placed inside the word for decay

parts.note: rust is the corrosion or decay of iron

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word that follows is dropped

parts.note: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Greek myth, hence oblivion
room in the sense of scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: A cryptic warning that a mistaken leader brings forgetting and wasted chances amid decline.
explanation.walkthrough: RULE THE ROOST is a corruption of the older phrase rule the roast, hence 'In error' in the definition. Lethe is the river of forgetting in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule the roost is to be in charge and lead others; 'In error' flags that the phrase is a mistaken form of rule the roast.

clue.text: What sewer carries is pretty fruity from the central regions

indicators.note: the central regions of words are their middles, so only the centre letters of each are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six-letter word
the two central letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A smelly drain's contents described with a wry, juicy adjective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' looks like a drain; it is someone who sews, who carries a needle case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and thread, the kind of thing a seamstress keeps to hand.

clue.text: Opening in kilt ridicule challenging mag

parts.note: Chambers gives spare as an opening in a garment, such as a slit in a kilt or skirt
to rib is to tease or mock

explanation.surface: Mocking a slit in someone's kilt in a provocative magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare Rib was a British feminist magazine published from 1972 to 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare Rib was a campaigning feminist magazine that challenged conventional attitudes.

clue.text: Naval officer's utter delight rounding the Kentish region?

indicators.note: to round something is to go around it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to purr is to utter a sound of contentment or delight
Kent lies in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A sailor's sheer joy at sailing round Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like an adjective meaning total; it is the verb to voice. Kent is a county in England's south-east corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A purser is the ship's officer in charge of accounts and supplies.

clue.text: To bask is in New Mexico's set of orthodox beliefs

parts.note: to sun oneself is to bask

indicators.note: the short verb is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NM is the postal abbreviation for New Mexico
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sunbathing as a New Mexico creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunnism is the orthodox mainstream branch of Islam, as distinct from Shia.

clue.text: Flower (Chinese), first from the right school

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for Chinese

indicators.note: reading from the right means going backwards against normal order

parts.note: first is number one
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A Chinese bloom, apparently the top choice of the correct school.
explanation.definitionFit: A chenopod is a plant of the goosefoot family, so a flowering plant broadly.

clue.text: Copper swells in recycled jeans?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
swells and toffs are both old slang for posh, fashionable people

explanation.surface: A police officer sees upper-class people wearing reworked denim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman and 'swells' a verb; both are nouns of other kinds here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutoffs are old jeans with the legs cut off to make shorts, a way of reusing worn trousers.

clue.text: Boater, say, to lie about reefer

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the combined pieces read upwards

parts.note: a boater is a straw hat
to fib is to tell a small lie

explanation.surface: A rower telling tales about a sailor's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boater' and 'reefer' both suggest boats; a reefer here is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A biftah is slang for a large cannabis cigarette, which is what a reefer is.

clue.text: Unbending stickler's point in trading place

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a mart is a market
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A rigid pedant making a point at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian who insists on rules being followed to the letter.

clue.text: Timber is extremely artificial

parts.note: too means excessively, extremely
art. is the abbreviation for artificial

explanation.surface: A complaint that some wood looks very fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooart, or tuart, is a Western Australian eucalyptus valued for its hard, durable wood.

clue.text: Row about what limits thankful claimant in the past

indicators.note: one piece goes about, that is around, the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundary letters, so only the first and last are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dispute over what restrains a grateful claimant from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Titler is an obsolete word for one who asserts a title or claim, hence an old-time claimant.

clue.text: Deaccession book from premium load

indicators.note: deaccessioning is a library or museum removing an item from its collection, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment, a premium
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A library disposing of a book to lighten its stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deaccession' sounds like library jargon, which fits 'book', but here it orders a letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, something one carries.

clue.text: Steals wheels from the south

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading from the south means from the bottom up

parts.note: spins and wheels both mean turns round

explanation.surface: A thief taking the wheels off a car in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a car's tyres; it is the verb to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To snip is to snatch or take sharply, so snips can mean steals.

clue.text: Mortal turned towards beguiling noise, no?

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off

indicators.note: to beguile is to deceive or lead astray, so the following letters are misled into a new order

parts.note: on as in moving on towards something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A human being drawn towards an alluring sound, like a sailor to the Sirens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mortal' seems to mean a human; it is the slang adjective for blind drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortal is slang for very drunk, and off one's onion describes someone out of their senses.

clue.text: Miss providing massage reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: to knead is to massage with the hands

explanation.surface: A young woman offering massages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman's title; it is the verb to feel the lack of.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to feel its absence and want it, which is to need it.

clue.text: In America wolf up bit of Thucydides

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: lobo is the American name for the grey wolf of the West

explanation.surface: An American wolf gobbling part of a Greek history book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' suggests a passage of text; it is a coin, and Thucydides was a Greek historian.
explanation.definitionFit: An obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, the money of Thucydides' day.

clue.text: Industrious colonist back outside state restaurant in the Aegean

indicators.note: the first piece goes on the outside of the second
going back means the insect word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ants are industrious insects living in colonies
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A hard-working settler returns to a Greek island eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant or tavern, typical of the Aegean islands.

clue.text: Faraday — outstanding type

parts.note: F is the symbol for the Faraday constant
ace means excellent, outstanding

explanation.surface: Michael Faraday praised as a brilliant sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding type' reads as one phrase about a person; the last word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing a face, or typeface, is a particular design of type.

clue.text: Daily work by Sergeant-Major on motivational research

parts.note: MR is the abbreviation for motivational research
SM is the abbreviation for Sergeant-Major
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A daily task carried out by an army sergeant-major using psychology research.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given in reverse: work comes by the sergeant-major, which is on the research. A daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Mop is a jokey British name for a charwoman, and a daily is a domestic cleaner.

clue.text: Shakespeare's mess is intractable

parts.note: the contraction 's stands for is
hard as in difficult to deal with

explanation.surface: The Bard's muddle proves hard to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers marks this sense as Shakespearean: a patch of cow dung, as in Macbeth's shard-borne beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare a shard is a cowpat, a dungy mess.

clue.text: Revamped tablets, such as may be charged in, eg, All Souls Buttery

definitions.text: such as may be charged in, eg, All Souls Buttery

indicators.note: something revamped has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reformulated pills sold over the counter at an Oxford college's food store.
explanation.walkthrough: All Souls is an Oxford college, and a buttery is a college store for food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford, battels are a college member's account for provisions and charges, settled each term.
